title: Territorial enforcement: egress corridor circuit and fallback model variant plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a deterministic enforcement path for region-locked requests (example: EU-only customers) that guarantees no cross-border egress, supports tenant-level allowlists/denylists, and provides safe fallback to locally-hosted model variants when capacity or model compatibility constraints occur.

Motivation: Several enterprise customers need strict territorial controls (EU data residency) plus fine-grained tenant permit/deny policies. Current routing is policy-driven but allows ambiguous failovers that may route a request outside the allowed boundary. We need an enforcement circuit that (1) verifies geographic constraints at gateway, (2) consults a light-weight policy decision service for tenant allowlists/denylists and tier routing, (3) executes deterministic fallback to pre-approved local model variants, and (4) emits auditable attestations proving residency.

Scope: This ticket covers design + runtime changes required to implement the enforcement circuit for EU-only tenancy and the fallback flow for model variant unavailability. Implementation will include request annotations, policy cache semantics, routing decision matrix, fallback prioritization, and end-to-end tests. It does NOT include UI tenant management (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: All inbound requests for tenants flagged as 'territory:EU' are tagged at the edge gateway with a signed residency enforcement header before any internal routing decision.

Policy Decision Service (PDS) responds within 50ms P95 with {allow|deny|route-tier|fallback-sequence} decisions for cached entries; cache TTL defaults to 30s and honors immediate invalidation on policy change push.

Routing layer never routes a request to a non-EU egress when tenant policy is 'EU-only'—if no compatible EU model variant exists, the request follows the fallback-sequence and either (a) invokes a sanitized local shim model, (b) places into a retry-queue with exponential backoff, or (c) returns a gated error with recommended mitigation steps.
All policy decisions and final egress endpoints are written to the audit log with tenant id, policy id, chosen model variant, latency, and a signed attest token for compliance review.
Integration test harness demonstrates simulated EU capacity depletion and confirms fallback order, observable metrics, and that no outbound egress crosses the EU boundary in any tested scenario.
tasks: Design decision doc: enforcement header format, signed attest token spec, and PDS interface
Runtime change: edge gateway injects residency header and performs initial local allowlist check
PDS: implement fast cache + invalidation API and tier routing response codes
Routing layer: enforce egress corridor — ensure model locator filters by region tag
Fallback engine: implement deterministic fallback sequence with priorities and local shim model hook
Telemetry: emit policy_decision, chosen_variant, and attest_token fields to console traces and audit logs
Tests: unit tests for routing predicates, integration test with synthetic EU capacity exhaustion, and chaos test for PDS outage
Docs: developer playbook for handling 'EU-only' tenant onboarding and migration runbook
notes: Design trade-offs: strong guarantee vs availability. Preference is to fail closed for compliance-bound tenants; however product may offer opt-in 'soft-fallback' where customers accept non-EU fallback with explicit consent (handled in another ticket).
We must avoid long tail latency introduced by synchronous PDS calls. Plan uses cache-first PDS with conservative TTL and asynchronous invalidation on policy updates.
Signed residency attest token should be HMACed by a KMS key scoped to the region; design doc will propose token payload minimal fields: tenant_id, policy_id, egress_region, timestamp, nonce.

Fallback variants: prioritize exact-architecture EU-hosted quantized variants, then reduced-context local shim (sanitization), then queued retry. Do NOT auto-fallback to non-EU hosted models for P0 compliance tenants.
Operational metrics to add: egress_blocked_rate, fallback_activation_rate, PDS_miss_rate, attest_token_generation_latency.
risks: Increased request latency if PDS cache miss occurs; mitigated by short TTL and local allowlist quick-path.
Operational complexity when customers change residency policies frequently—need quick invalidation path and visible deployment pipeline for policy pushes.
Edge cases where hybrid deployments span EU and non-EU hardware; require strict model tagging and periodic audits to prevent mis-tagged variants.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement header + local allowlist check, PDS mock responses, and shadow routing for 5 internal tenants in eu-west region
Phase 2 (limited): enable enforcement for a small set of pilot customers with legal sign-off; enable audit tokens and long-term log retention
Phase 3 (general): enable for all customers with EU residency flag; expose metrics and console alerts; provide migration docs
Rollback: on any evidence of cross-border egress misrouting, system toggles enforcement to 'audit-only' mode and notifies SRE and legal teams
